 Appearance:

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of preferring the present application under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the applicant - accused seeks to invoke the inherent powers of this Court, praying to quash and set-aside the First Information Report being I-C.R. No. 42 of 2014 registered with the Agathala Police Station, District Banaskantha, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3(C), 4, 8, 17 and 29 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, as well as all other consequential proceedings arising pursuant thereto.

2. On 18.12.2025, this Court has passed the following order:-
"1.

Learned advocate Mr. Premdeepsinh Jadeja appears NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26738/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined and submits that he Padmabhai Jivabhai Patel (Kandli/ ... vs State Of Gujarat on 2 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195250114/
1 has instructions to appear on behalf of the respondent no.2 - complainant.

sentences.text: He is permitted to file his appearance.
Registry shall accept his vakalatnama.
2. Learned advocate Mr.Kishore Prajapati for the applicant has submitted that the matter is settled between the parties.

The complainant, who herself is the victim, is personally present in the Court and has filed an affidavit, inter alia, contending that she has already got married with the present applicant and has been blessed with two children, namely, Dharmik and Kailash.
3. Learned advocate Mr. Kishore Prajapati has further submitted that the birth certificates of both the children are also placed on record.
4. Upon bare perusal of the birth certificates, it prima facie appears that the names of the present applicant and the victim have not been shown as the parents of the children.

5. Learned APP is, therefore, directed to verify the genuineness of the certificates,
through the Investigating Officer, by the next date of hearing.

6. Stand over to 13.01.2026."
3.

Today, when the matter is called out, learned advocate appearing for the applicant has submitted a copy of the application for correction in the name of the parents in the birth certificate of the children submitted to the Registrar of Birth & Death, Damnagar Municipality by the complainant /
victim, as well as the attested copy of her marriage certificate with the applicant.
The same are ordered to be taken on record.

4. It is submitted that at the time of the alleged incident, the complainant, who herself is the victim,
was aged about 17 years, whereas the applicant-accused was aged about 22 years.
It is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26738/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined submitted that since both were in love, after registration of the impugned FIR, they got married.

It appears that the marriage has also been registered before the Marriage Registrar, Bhayavadar, District Rajkot, and since then, both of the them are residing together and out of the said wedlock, they have also been blessed with two children.

Learned advocate Mr. Jadeja appearing for the complainant has also pointed out to the affidavit filed by the complainant / victim dated 09.12.2025, wherein, the complainant has categorically stated that with the intervention of the friends, family members and community people, the dispute has been amicably resolved with the applicant and there is no ill-will or any grievance amongst them.

5. Considering the issue involved in the present application as well as considering the fact that the dispute has been amicably resolved between the parties, with the consent of the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, the present application is taken up for final disposal.

sentences.text: RULE returnable forthwith.

Learned APP Ms. Krina Calla waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent no.1 - State and learned advocate Mr. Premdeep V. Jadeja waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent no.2 - complainant.
7.

Learned advocate for the applicant-accused has submitted that since the dispute has been amicably resolved between the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26738/2025 ORDER DATED:
02/03/2026 undefined parties, the application may be allowed and the impugned FIR may be quashed and set-aside.

8. The complainant, who was personally present in the Court on the last occasion on 18.12.2025, has categorically stated before this Court that she has no objection if the application is allowed and the impugned FIR is quashed and set-aside.
Thus, it appears from the aforesaid that sending the applicant-accused to face the trial would be nothing but a futile exercise and would amount to abuse of process of law.

9. The relevant paragraphs of the affidavit dated 09.12.2025, filed by the complainant / victim, read thus :
"1. That, I have been read over and explained the contents of memo of application in Gujarati and I have understood the same properly.
I say that, as I am the original complainant and respondent No. 2 herein and as I am conversant with the facts of the case, I am competent to file this affidavit on my behalf.

2. At the outset I say and submit that, the complaint being C.R. No. I-42 of 2014 dated 11.06.2014 registered before Agthala Police Station, District Banaskantha for the offences punishable u/s. 363, 366, 376 of IPC and u/s. 3(C), 4, 8, 17 and 29 of POCSO Act of GP Act by me.

The said complaint is registered in heat moment and on account of pressure of uncle in fact I am in love with applicant.
3. At the outset, I say and submit that after complaint the village peoples and elderly persons of society gathered and amicably settled the dispute and the undersigned happily married with the applicant and two child Viz. Dharmik and Kailash born out of the said wedlock at above village and now I do not want to proceed further the FIR dodged by me as we are happily residing together.
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances application NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26738/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined which is going to be filed by the applicant is deserves to be allowed in terms of prayer made therein."

10. The relevant paragraphs of the further affidavit dated 13.01.2026, filed by the complainant /
victim, read thus :
"1.
That, I have been read over and explained the contents of memo of application in Gujarati and I have understood the same properly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That, after filling the affidavit in main matter there is latest development and the same are required to be placed on record and therefore the present additional affidavit is filed.
3. That, this Hon'ble Court orally directed to keep the father of respondent No.2 present.

I say and submit that, my father is mentally ill and therefore I contacted my mother and brother and requested to remain present before this Hon'ble court,
initially they are ready and willing to remain present and file affidavit but, later on they refused on the ground that "      " and hence, the respondent No.2 unable to call their parents before this Hon'ble court.
4. That, after the date of hearing the undersigned applied for rectification in the birth certificate of both son by correcting names of parents and to that effect sworn affidavit on stamp paper and the process is going on before the registration authority.
Copy of affidavit is enclosed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE-F to this additional affidavit.
5.

At the outset, I say and submit that now I am happily married with the applicant and have two children Viz. Dharmik and Kailash born out of the said wedlock at above village and now I do not want to proceed further the FIR lodged by me as we are happily residing together.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances the application filed by the applicant deserves to be allowed in terms of prayer made therein."
11.

Having heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties as well as considering the facts and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26738/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/03/2026 undefined circumstances arising out of the present application and taking into consideration the decisions rendered in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303,
Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, Nikhil Merchant vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Another, reported in (2009) 1 GLH 31, Manoj Sharma vs. State & Others,
reported in (2009) 1 GLH 190, and Narinder Singh & Others vs. State of Punjab & Another, reported in (2014) 2 Crime 67 (SC) as well as State of Haryana vs. Bhajanlal, reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, it appears that further continuation of the criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR against the applicant-accused would be nothing but unnecessary harassment to the applicant- accused.

Hence, to secure the ends of justice, the impugned FIR and all other consequential proceedings arising pursuant thereto are required to be quashed and set-aside in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
12.

13. Rule made absolute.
